messages:
oliver: Heads-up — we need a concise contingency/runbook for canary failures that need automatic reroute. Yesterday's canary hit a memory cliff and took ~2m to recover. We should define precise fallback rules instead of ad-hoc ops calls.

mari: +1. Can we scope: (1) metric triggers, (2) failover targets, (3) cooldowns & probes, (4) telem + pagering?

kevin: I think the three-tier target model worked well in theory: primary model > quantized fallback > cached responses. Question: do we allow cross-region fallback or restrict to same region?

oliver: prefer same region by default for latency. cross-region only as last resort (and with explicit opt-in for customers that need it).

sarah: For metric triggers: p95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 30s OR error-rate > 1% for 1m OR memory OOMs on host. Those should auto-trip.

mari: add sustained token generation stalls (kernel hangs) — if token throughput drops by >40% vs baseline for 30s.

kevin: Agreed. Also need a short TTL so we don't flip-flop: a min-failover duration + an exponential backoff probe schedule. I suggest min duration 2m, probe at 30s, 90s, 3m, then 6m.

oliver: sounds reasonable. Let's capture it as a policy snippet so infra can implement. Example config idea:

```yaml
failover_policy:
  metrics:
    latency_p95_multiplier: 1.5
    latency_window: 30s
    error_rate_threshold: 0.01
    error_window: 60s
  targets:
    - name: model-quantized-v1
      reason: lower memory / faster kernels
    - name: model-cache-fallback
      reason: prefix cache / cached completions
  min_failover_duration: 120s
  probe_schedule: [30s, 90s, 180s, 360s]
  allow_cross_region: false
```

sarah: Nice. A couple of tradeoffs: quantized model may reduce quality. We need acceptance checks in the routing layer: sample 1% of requests to the quantized variant and run quick evals (or check similarity metrics) before full traffic shift.

mari: We already have quick-eval infra. Implementation: when failover triggers, route 90% to fallback, keep 10% to primary for continuous quality gating. If similarity drops below threshold for 3 probes, auto-rollback to primary and escalate.

kevin: For incidents where primary is dying (OOM), maybe flip to 100% fallback immediately but mark incident state = "forced-failover" and notify oncall with high priority. That avoids partials that also die.

oliver: Good point. We should encode severity levels: 
- soft: performance regression -> gradual 90/10 -> 100%
- hard: OOM / host instability -> immediate 100%

mari: Telemetry: route-change events must be annotated with cause, metrics at flip time, and probe deltas. Add a short-lived trace-id header to correlate across services.

sarah: Also need to prevent cascading cost blowups: if fallback is more expensive (e.g., CPU-bound multi-node), enforce a cost cap per customer — if exceeded, fallback to cached or degrade feature.

kevin: Operationally: implement a state machine with states: NORMAL -> SOFT_FAILOVER -> PROBING -> HARD_FAILOVER -> COOLDOWN -> ROLLBACK. Each transition has guards and timers.

oliver: Agree. Small checklist for the runbook doc we want:
- Trigger definitions (metrics + windows)
- Target list and ordering
- Probe cadence and sampling fraction
- Min durations and cooldowns
- Severity classifications and oncall actions
- Cross-region policy + data residency notes
- Cost safety caps and autoscaling considerations
- Logging/trace annotations + dashboard panels
- Playbook scripts for manual override (flags / route pin)

mari: Also include a simple CLI snippet for force-failover / revert:

```bash
# force to quantized model for customer X
rictl route set --customer X --route /generate --model model-quantized-v1 --reason "ops_force_failover"
# revert
rictl route revert --customer X --route /generate
```

sarah: Notifications: when entering HARD_FAILOVER -> page oncall, open incident ticket automatically, annotate release if canary was recent. For SOFT_FAILOVER -> only slack alert to #eng-oncall and #product-alerts.

kevin: One more: we should avoid dual reads of KV cache during failover causing stampeding. Add a short jitter and local in-memory guard to ensure only one bootstrap cold fill per prefix.

oliver: Action items: (1) mari to draft runbook doc + config schema, (2) kevin to sketch state-machine proto, (3) sarah to add probes + quick-eval hook into infra, (4) oliver to create dashboard templates and alert rules.

mari: I'll draft and post a PR by EOD tomorrow.

deploy-bot: Canary for model-2026-03-14-quantized started in us-west-2 at 2034567922

oliver: ok thanks. we'll iterate on the doc and link infra PRs into the canary run.

kevin: FYI, I'll prototype the state-machine in the feature branch and include unit tests for the timers.

sarah: I'll work on the gating similarity metric and add a low-cost hashing compare first to avoid heavy evals.

oliver: Great. Let's reconvene async on the PRs. If anyone wants to add edge cases (billing, tenant pinning, golden-traffic), drop them into the doc. :thumbsup:
